name: Palais Présidentiel et Lac aux Crocodiles
subtitle: Historic presidential compound encircled by artificial moats teeming with legendary sacred West African crocodiles.

facts.label: Built
facts.value: 1970s as the official inland palace of Félix Houphouët-Boigny

facts.label: Famous feature
facts.value: Interconnected artificial lakes home to hundreds of sacred West African crocodiles

facts.label: Tradition
facts.value: Daily feeding ritual at dusk by traditional Baoulé guardians attracting civic observers

parts.text: The presidential palace complex of Yamoussoukro, surrounded by extensive perimeter walls and a series of artificial moats and lakes. The compound was created in the 1970s around the ancestral homestead of Côte d'Ivoire's founding president, Félix Houphouët-Boigny. The palace lakes are internationally known for harboring hundreds of West African crocodiles, introduced by Houphouët-Boigny as symbols of protective power and traditional Baoulé kingship, fed meat each evening at sunset by hereditary custodians.

gaps: Security access to the interior palace residence is restricted to official delegations.
